items.detail: The **S&P 500** gained about 1.2% on the week to 7,811.54, and the Nasdaq rose about 0.7% to 27,366.17, after both set records Tuesday.
items.why: Fading Fed hike bets after the jobs miss lifted tech early, and an oil spike midweek cut the gains.

items.detail: Brent swung from below $100 to about **$106** Thursday, then eased to near $103 Friday, and still finished the week higher.
items.why: Iranian attacks on Hormuz shipping and US strike fears hit supply until Trump ruled out strikes before the midterms.

items.detail: AI chip stocks dragged the Nasdaq down **1.25%** Thursday, then recovered Friday, while strong auctions pulled the 10-year yield back from 5.35%, its highest since 2002.
items.why: A report that OpenAI's revenue was overstated hit chips until OpenAI said it expects $70 billion by year-end.

items.detail: Emerging markets rallied early in the week, then the selloff hit Asia, with **Korea's Kospi** falling three straight days before Hong Kong bounced 1.79% Friday.
items.why: Higher oil and a stronger dollar from Hormuz tensions hurt oil-importing emerging markets until Friday's relief.

items.detail: The **Nifty** ended about 0.4% higher at 22,520.45, after hitting a 52-week low Thursday, as the RBI raised rates to 5.5%.
items.why: The RBI's first hike since 2023, higher crude and steady foreign selling weighed until oil eased Friday.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** fell about 0.9% on the week to 2,806.98, lagging record-setting large caps and staying about 9% below its August high.
items.why: Long-term Treasury yields near 24-year highs hit debt-heavy small companies harder than megacap tech.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** failed twice to break $87,000, then slid four straight days to about **$82,600**, briefly dipping below $81,000.
items.why: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $729 million over two sessions, the biggest outflows since June.

items.detail: **Ether** fell from about $2,716 to around **$2,500**, after touching a midweek low near $2,406.
items.why: Eight straight days of ether ETF outflows outweighed the Glamsterdam upgrade's successful testnet launch.

items.detail: **Solana** broke out of its $120 range and slid to about **$110** by Friday.
items.why: Bitcoin's slide, steady Solana ETF outflows and Standard Chartered cutting its target to $250 from $310 drove the drop.

items.detail: **Spot gold** hit a two-month low of $4,104 Tuesday, then recovered to near **$4,194** Friday, briefly topping $4,200.
items.why: Gold fell as yields hit 2002 highs, then gained as yields eased, the dollar weakened and Iran fears returned.

crossCuttingTheme: Oil moved every market this week: the Hormuz attacks pushed Brent and inflation fears up, which kept long-term yields near 2002 highs, and stocks, emerging markets and gold recovered only when Trump's Iran pledge brought crude back down.
